title: 556. Discrete Mathematics, Counting & Graph Theory: Binomial Coefficients
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a small binomial coefficient from its factorial formula.
questions.question: The binomial coefficient is defined by \(\binom{n}{k}=\dfrac{n!}{k!\,(n-k)!}\). What is \(\binom{5}{2}\)?
questions.explanation: \(\binom{5}{2}=\dfrac{5!}{2!\,3!}=\dfrac{120}{2\cdot 6}=10\). The number \(20=\dfrac{5!}{3!}\) omits the factor \(2!\) in the denominator.
questions.hint: Both \(k!\) and \((n-k)!\) appear in the denominator.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a binomial coefficient with lower index zero.
questions.question: What is \(\binom{9}{0}\)?
questions.explanation: By the formula, \(\binom{9}{0}=\dfrac{9!}{0!\,9!}=1\), because \(0!=1\). In counting terms, there is exactly one way to choose nothing from \(9\) objects: take none. The value is not \(0\).
questions.hint: Recall the value of \(0!\), or count the ways to choose no object.

questions.concept: A coefficient with lower index four
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a binomial coefficient by cancelling factorials.
questions.question: What is \(\binom{9}{4}\)?
questions.explanation: \(\binom{9}{4}=\dfrac{9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot 6}{4\cdot 3\cdot 2\cdot 1}=\dfrac{3024}{24}=126\). The number \(3024\) is only the numerator; the division by \(4!\) is still required.
questions.hint: Write four decreasing factors in the numerator and \(4!\) in the denominator.

questions.learningObjective: Use the symmetry of binomial coefficients.
questions.question: Which binomial coefficient is equal to \(\binom{15}{4}\)?
questions.explanation: Choosing \(4\) objects from \(15\) is the same as choosing the \(11\) objects that are left out, so \(\binom{15}{4}=\binom{15}{11}\). In general \(\binom{n}{k}=\binom{n}{n-k}\). The coefficient \(\binom{15}{5}=3003\) differs from \(\binom{15}{4}=1365\).
questions.hint: Compare choosing objects with choosing the objects that are not taken.

questions.concept: A coefficient with lower index two
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a binomial coefficient with lower index two.
questions.question: What is \(\binom{20}{2}\)?
questions.explanation: \(\binom{20}{2}=\dfrac{20\cdot 19}{2}=190\). The number \(380=20\cdot 19\) is the number of ordered pairs; the division by \(2!\) has been forgotten.

questions.concept: From one coefficient to the next
questions.learningObjective: Compute a binomial coefficient from its neighbour in the same row.
questions.question: Given that \(\binom{10}{3}=120\), what is \(\binom{10}{4}\)?
questions.explanation: Neighbouring coefficients satisfy \(\binom{n}{k+1}=\binom{n}{k}\cdot\dfrac{n-k}{k+1}\). With \(n=10\) and \(k=3\): \(\binom{10}{4}=120\cdot\dfrac{7}{4}=210\). The number \(160=120\cdot\dfrac{4}{3}\) uses the wrong ratio.
questions.hint: Compare the factorial formulas of the two coefficients and cancel the common factors.

questions.concept: The largest coefficient in a row
questions.learningObjective: Locate the largest binomial coefficient for a fixed upper index.
questions.question: For which value of \(k\) is \(\binom{8}{k}\) largest?
questions.explanation: The coefficients \(\binom{8}{k}\) for \(k=0,\dots,8\) are \(1,8,28,56,70,56,28,8,1\). They increase up to the middle and then decrease symmetrically, so the largest is \(\binom{8}{4}=70\). At \(k=8\) the value is only \(1\).
questions.hint: List the whole row, or use its symmetry.

questions.learningObjective: Recognise an identity for a binomial coefficient multiplied by its lower index.
questions.question: For \(1\le k\le n\), which expression is equal to \(k\binom{n}{k}\)?
questions.explanation: Count the ways to choose a committee of \(k\) from \(n\) people and then a chair from the committee: \(k\binom{n}{k}\). Alternatively choose the chair first, in \(n\) ways, and then the other \(k-1\) members from the remaining \(n-1\) people: \(n\binom{n-1}{k-1}\). Both count the same thing. A check with \(n=4\), \(k=2\) gives \(2\cdot 6=12=4\cdot 3\), while \(n\binom{n}{k-1}=4\cdot 4=16\).
questions.hint: Test each candidate with small values such as \(n=4\) and \(k=2\).

questions.learningObjective: Solve an equation relating two binomial coefficients.
questions.question: For which positive integer \(n\) is \(\binom{n}{3}=4\binom{n}{2}\)?
questions.explanation: Dividing, \(\dfrac{\binom{n}{3}}{\binom{n}{2}}=\dfrac{n-2}{3}\). Setting this equal to \(4\) gives \(n-2=12\), so \(n=14\). Check: \(\binom{14}{3}=364\) and \(4\binom{14}{2}=4\cdot 91=364\). For \(n=12\) the two sides are \(220\) and \(264\).
questions.hint: Form the quotient of the two coefficients and simplify it.

questions.learningObjective: Use symmetry to solve an equation between binomial coefficients.
questions.question: For which positive integer \(n\) is \(\binom{n}{2}=\binom{n}{5}\)?
questions.explanation: Within one row, \(\binom{n}{j}=\binom{n}{k}\) with \(j\ne k\) happens exactly when \(j+k=n\), by symmetry and because the row increases up to its middle. So \(n=2+5=7\): \(\binom{7}{2}=\binom{7}{5}=21\). For \(n=10\), \(\binom{10}{2}=45\) but \(\binom{10}{5}=252\).
questions.hint: Two different positions in the same row hold equal coefficients when they are mirror images of each other.
